segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have part two of a very important and very valuable series about giving presentations.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们有一个非常重要且非常有价值的系列节目的第二部分。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: As you well know, we started this series.
segments.zh: 众所周知，我们开始了这个系列。

segments.en: It's a ten-part series and today we're going to talk about sales and charts and graphs and more or less explaining maybe a PowerPoint presentation.
segments.zh: 这是一个十部分的系列，今天我们将讨论销售和图表和图表，或多或少地解释可能的 PowerPoint 演示文稿。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And some wonderful ways of talking about changes in markets and marketing.
segments.zh: 以及一些谈论市场和营销变化的绝妙方式。

segments.en: So let's take a listen to today's dialogue and we'll be back in a moment to talk about what you've heard.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听听今天的对话，我们稍后会回来谈论你所听到的。

segments.en: As all of you are well aware, competition in the laptop computer sector is intense.
segments.zh: 大家都知道，笔记本电脑领域的竞争非常激烈。

segments.en: We continue to fight with our competitors for market share and this is the case both in the developed markets in the West as well as more developing markets in Asia and Africa.
segments.zh: 我们继续与我们的竞争对手争夺市场份额，无论是在西方发达市场，还是亚洲和非洲的发展中市场。

segments.en: You may ask yourself, why is this market so cutthroat?
segments.zh: 你可能会问自己，为什么这个市场如此残酷？

segments.en: Well, the answer is simple.
segments.zh: 嗯，答案很简单。

segments.en: There is a huge untapped potential market out there with a huge untapped potential for profit.
segments.zh: 有一个巨大的未开发的潜在市场，具有巨大的未开发的利润潜力。

segments.en: If I bring up the first graph here, it shows the increase in terms of number of computer owners across the globe.
segments.zh: 请看这里的第一张图，它显示了全球电脑用户数量的增长。

segments.en: As you can see, in the 1980s, computer ownership amounted to around 0.5% of the total world population.
segments.zh: 如图所示，上世纪八十年代，拥有电脑的人约占全球总人口的百分之零点五。

segments.en: Since the 1990s, computer ownership has risen dramatically.
segments.zh: 自上世纪九十年代以来，电脑拥有率显著上升。

segments.en: In the new millennium, we saw an even larger explosion in computer owners with figures rising to around 4-5%, an increase of 1000% compared with the 1980s.
segments.zh: 在新千年，我们看到计算机用户的数量爆炸式增长，数字上升到 4-5% 左右，与 1980 年代相比增长了 1000%。

segments.en: If we move on to discuss the figures for China specifically, we can see in chart B that the overall figure for computer ownership stands at around 60 million, which represents a huge increase in a very short time period.
segments.zh: 再具体看看中国的数据，图表 B 显示，电脑用户总数约为六千万，短时间内增长非常迅速。

segments.en: Now of course, 60 million is just a drop in the ocean if you compare the total population of China.
segments.zh: 当然，和中国总人口相比，六千万不过是沧海一粟。

segments.en: And this is a key reason why the personal computer market is such a hot market.
segments.zh: 这是个人电脑市场如此火爆的一个关键原因。

segments.en: For us at Alpha, and of course for all of our competitors as well, we have millions of potential customers who are looking to join the internet generation.
segments.zh: 对于我们在 Alpha 的我们，当然对于我们所有的竞争对手来说，我们有数以百万计的潜在客户希望加入互联网一代。

segments.en: If we do this right, we really can reap huge rewards in a very short time frame.
segments.zh: 如果我们做对了，我们真的可以在很短的时间内获得巨大的回报。

segments.en: I'd now like to move on to discuss the X420 brand itself and compare and contrast with some of our key competitors.
segments.zh: 我现在想继续讨论 X420 品牌本身，并与我们的一些主要竞争对手进行比较和对比。

segments.en: Alright we're back so now let's start with Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，所以现在让我们从语言外卖开始。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, so in the first part of what Mr. Ford is saying, he mentions something called market share.
segments.zh: 好的，所以在福特先生所说的第一部分，他提到了一种叫做市场份额的东西。

segments.en: Now Margot, what is market share?
segments.zh: 现在玛戈特，什么是市场份额？

segments.en: That's right, everyone is competing for market share and this is basically a small portion of your available market.
segments.zh: 没错，每个人都在争夺市场份额，这基本上只是您可用市场的一小部分。

segments.en: So for example, if you sell perfumes, women's perfume, then your market share is maybe women who are 18 to 35 years old in your city or in your town or in your country.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，如果您出售香水、女性香水，那么您的市场份额可能是在您所在城市、城镇或您所在国家/地区的 18 至 35 岁女性。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: Right, so when we're talking about market share because we're sharing a piece of this big pie, we're going to talk about that in terms of a percentage, so 30% or 15%.
segments.zh: 是的，所以当我们谈论市场份额时，因为我们正在分享这个大蛋糕的一部分，我们将以百分比的百分比来讨论这个问题，所以 30% 或 15%。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: I think maybe one of the clearest examples is Coca-Cola has I think maybe a 60% market share of the carbonated beverages market.
segments.zh: 我认为也许最明显的例子之一是可口可乐，我认为碳酸饮料市场的市场份额可能占 60%。

segments.en: Interesting, so you could say that Apple has a 50% market share of the personal computing industry.
segments.zh: 有趣的是，你可以说苹果在个人计算行业中拥有 50% 的市场份额。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Very good, so this is what we refer to as market share.
segments.zh: 非常好，所以这就是我们所说的市场份额。

segments.en: Now as we continue to talk about markets, we have two very interesting words when we refer to a developed market and a developing market.
segments.zh: 现在，当我们继续谈论市场时，当我们提到发达市场和发展中市场时，我们有两个非常有趣的词。

segments.en: Okay so a developed market is something that has been polished and grown over time.
segments.zh: 好吧，发达市场是随着时间的推移而被打磨和发展的。

segments.en: Perhaps we talk about the developed world being Western Europe and America, but then we have developing markets and those are markets that are still trying to figure out kind of what's going on.
segments.zh: 也许我们谈论发达国家是西欧和美国，但我们有发展中的市场，而这些市场仍在试图弄清楚正在发生的事情。

segments.en: They're growing.
segments.zh: 他们正在成长。

segments.en: They're usually growing much faster than a developed market.
segments.zh: 它们的增长速度通常比发达市场快得多。

segments.en: That's right, so again when we're talking about maybe computers, we consider for example the United States a developed market.
segments.zh: 没错，所以当我们谈论可能的计算机时，我们会认为美国是一个发达的市场。

segments.en: Many people already have a computer or express the desire to buy one and so maybe a developing market are some of the African countries where they're still growing and so now they're beginning to purchase more and more computers.
segments.zh: 许多人已经拥有一台电脑或表达了购买一台计算机的愿望，因此发展中的市场可能是他们仍在发展的一些非洲国家，因此现在他们开始购买越来越多的计算机。

segments.en: Okay so developed and developing, two different ways to describe markets.
segments.zh: 好的，发展和发展，两种不同的描述市场的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Now after that we hear this phrase cutthroat.
segments.zh: 现在，我们听到这句话很残忍。

segments.en: So someone asks why is this market so cutthroat?
segments.zh: 所以有人问为什么这个市场如此残酷？

segments.en: What does this mean?
segments.zh: 这是什么意思？

segments.en: A cutthroat business or a cutthroat industry.
segments.zh: 残酷的企业或残酷的行业。

segments.en: It means that it's very, very competitive.
segments.zh: 这意味着它非常非常有竞争力。

segments.en: Okay so cutthroat, we're actually talking about maybe having a knife and cutting someone else's throat, but it's just a metaphor.
segments.zh: 好吧，这么残忍，我们实际上是在谈论可能有一把刀并割伤别人的喉咙，但这只是一个隐喻。

segments.en: It's a way of saying yes, this is very competitive.
segments.zh: 这是一种说是的方式，这是非常有竞争力的。

segments.en: So you're not actually cutting someone's throat.
segments.zh: 所以你实际上并没有割断别人的喉咙。

segments.en: Right, everyone is fighting for that market share so it's very cutthroat.
segments.zh: 是的，每个人都在为这个市场份额而战，所以它非常残酷。

segments.en: Everyone is fighting very, very hard, but you're not literally killing someone or cutting their throats.
segments.zh: 每个人都非常非常努力地战斗，但你并没有真正杀死某人或割断他们的喉咙。

segments.en: You could even use this to talk about a sporting event.
segments.zh: 你甚至可以用它来谈论体育赛事。

segments.en: You could say it was a cutthroat game.
segments.zh: 你可以说这是一个残酷的游戏。

segments.en: That's right, that's right.
segments.zh: 没错，没错。

segments.en: So anything that's very competitive or very close.
segments.zh: 所以任何非常有竞争力或非常接近的东西。

segments.en: So to finish off language takeaway when Mr. Ford was towards the end of his presentation, he said that the rewards could be very, very big in a very short time frame.
segments.zh: 因此，当福特先生在他的演讲即将结束时完成语言外卖时，他说奖励可能在很短的时间内非常非常大。

segments.en: So when we say the word time frame, we mean period of time.
segments.zh: 因此，当我们说单词时间框架时，我们指的是时间段。

segments.en: It's not like 2 p.m.
segments.zh: 这不像下午 2 点。

segments.en: It's like from May to June, we have this short time frame.
segments.zh: 就像从五月到六月，我们有这么短的时间框架。

segments.en: It's only 2 months long.
segments.zh: 只有2个月的时间。

segments.en: So time frame is a window or a period.
segments.zh: 所以时间框架是一个窗口或一个周期。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is what he is referring to is that in a very short period or in this period of time, they could make a lot of money, a time frame.
segments.zh: 所以这就是他所指的是，在很短的时间内或在这段时间里，他们可以赚很多钱，一个时间框架。

segments.en: But how long would a long time frame be?
segments.zh: 但是长的时间框架会持续多长时间？

segments.en: Maybe a couple of years.
segments.zh: 也许几年。

segments.en: All right, so you can have a short time frame and a long time frame.
segments.zh: 好的，所以你可以有一个短的时间框架和一个长的时间框架。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in today's dialogue, we heard Mr. Ford talk about some numbers.

segments.zh: 他说，数字达到 4-5% 左右，我们的总体增长率为 1000%。

segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: So what's a phrase, an increase of?

segments.en: Very very common when you're talking about growth of maybe revenue or when you're talking about the growth of a company or sales for example.
segments.zh: 当您谈论可能的收入增长或例如谈论公司或销售额的增长时，这是非常非常常见的。

segments.en: So it's important to remember here that this is a fixed phrase.
segments.zh: 因此，重要的是要记住这是一个固定的短语。

segments.en: We say an increase of 10% or an increase of 30%.
segments.zh: 我们说增加了 10% 或增加了 30%。

segments.en: But you can use the same phrase with drops in percentages or money.
segments.zh: 但是您可以使用相同的短语来减少百分比或金钱。

segments.en: So you can say a decrease of 10%.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说减少了 10%。

segments.en: That's right.

segments.zh: 对比是它们有何不同，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So let's use an example.
segments.zh: 所以让我们用一个例子。

segments.zh: 也许我们可以说百事可乐和可口可乐。

segments.zh: 让我们比较和对比。

segments.zh: 所以它们都是碳酸饮料。

segments.en: They are both sweet.
segments.zh: 他们都很甜。

segments.zh: 但我会说可口可乐的味道更像修剪。

segments.en: So that would be a contrasting characteristic of Coca-Cola is that maybe it tastes a little bit sweeter.
segments.zh: 所以这将是可口可乐的一个对比特征，也许它的味道可能更甜一点。

segments.en: It does.
segments.zh: 确实更甜一些。

segments.en: And you could also say it's easier to find Coca-Cola.
segments.zh: 你也可以说找到可口可乐更容易。

segments.en: Pepsi is less easy to find sometimes.
segments.zh: 百事可乐有时不太容易找到。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Another way that they're different.
segments.zh: 另一种方式是它们不同。

segments.en: To compare and contrast is to point out how two things are similar and how they're different.
segments.zh: 比较和对比就是指出两件事有何相似之处以及它们有何不同。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we've had a lot of interesting phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以我们在那里有很多有趣的短语。

segments.en: I think very useful if you're talking about business and marketing and sales.
segments.zh: 如果您谈论的是商业、营销和销售，我认为非常有用。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to our dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不上次听我们的对话。

segments.en: As all of you are well aware, competition in the laptop computer sector is intense.
segments.zh: 大家都知道，笔记本电脑领域的竞争非常激烈。

segments.en: We continue to fight with our competitors for market share.
segments.zh: 我们继续与竞争对手争夺市场份额。

segments.en: And this is the case both in the developed markets in the West as well as more developing markets in Asia and Africa.
segments.zh: 无论是在西方的发达市场，还是亚洲和非洲的发展中国家，情况都是如此。

segments.en: You may ask yourself, why is this market so cutthroat?
segments.zh: 你可能会问自己，为什么这个市场如此残酷？

segments.en: Well, the answer is simple.
segments.zh: 嗯，答案很简单。

segments.en: There's a huge untapped potential market out there with a huge untapped potential for profit.
segments.zh: 有一个巨大的未开发的潜在市场，具有巨大的未开发的利润潜力。

segments.en: If I bring up the first graph here, it shows the increase in terms of number of computer owners across the globe.
segments.zh: 请看这里的第一张图，它显示了全球电脑用户数量的增长。

segments.en: As you can see, in the 1980s, computer ownership amounted to around 0.5% of the total world population.
segments.zh: 如图所示，上世纪八十年代，拥有电脑的人约占全球总人口的百分之零点五。

segments.en: Since the 1990s, computer ownership has risen dramatically.
segments.zh: 自上世纪九十年代以来，电脑拥有率显著上升。

segments.en: In the new millennium, we saw an even larger explosion in computer owners with figures rising to around 4 to 5%, an increase of 1000% compared with the 1980s.
segments.zh: 在新的千年中，我们看到计算机所有者的爆炸性更大，数字上升到 4% 到 5% 左右，与 1980 年代相比增加了 1000%。

segments.en: If we move on to discuss the figures for China specifically, we can see in chart B that the overall figure for computer ownership stands at around 60 million, which represents a huge increase in a very short time period.
segments.zh: 再具体看看中国的数据，图表 B 显示，电脑用户总数约为六千万，短时间内增长非常迅速。

segments.en: Now of course, 60 million is just a drop in the ocean if you compare the total population of China.
segments.zh: 当然，和中国总人口相比，六千万不过是沧海一粟。

segments.en: And this is a key reason why the personal computer market is such a hot market.
segments.zh: 这是个人电脑市场如此火爆的一个关键原因。

segments.en: For us at Alpha, and of course for all of our competitors as well, we have millions of potential customers who are looking to join the internet generation.
segments.zh: 对于我们在 Alpha 的我们，当然对于我们所有的竞争对手来说，我们有数以百万计的潜在客户希望加入互联网一代。

segments.en: If we do this right, we really can reap huge rewards in a very short time frame.
segments.zh: 如果我们做对了，我们真的可以在很短的时间内获得巨大的回报。

segments.en: I'd now like to move on to discuss the X420 brand itself and compare and contrast with some of our key competitors.
segments.zh: 我现在想继续讨论 X420 品牌本身，并与我们的一些主要竞争对手进行比较和对比。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So, as we mentioned, this is just a part of our presentation series.
segments.zh: 因此，正如我们所提到的，这只是我们演示系列的一部分。

segments.en: We're going to keep on talking with Mr. Ford as he discusses business and a lot of other very interesting and useful skills for talking in public.
segments.zh: 我们将继续与福特先生讨论业务以及在公共场合交谈的许多其他非常有趣和有用的技能。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And the goal of this series is to help you feel better when you're giving a presentation in English.
segments.zh: 本系列的目标是帮助您在用英语进行演示时感觉更好。

segments.en: We all know it's very, very hard to talk in English when you're still learning, but it's even harder to talk alone, to give a speech or a presentation.
segments.zh: 我们都知道，当您还在学习时，用英语交谈非常非常困难，但单独交谈、发表演讲或演讲更难。

segments.en: And so the point of this series is to really give you those skills and to help teach you some of the key phrases and words that you'll be using in your presentations in the future.
segments.zh: 因此，本系列的重点是真正为您提供这些技能，并帮助您教您未来将在演示中使用的一些关键短语和单词。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if you have any questions or any doubts, we are always available at EnglishPod.com and we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您有任何疑问或疑问，我们随时可以在 Englishpod.com 上看到我们，我们会在那里见到每个人。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
